label: Income and ancestry variables missing
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis needs a community-level income exposure (e.g. census-tract median income, ADI, zip-level income) and a genetic-ancestry covariate, but the provided clinical tables (patient: PATIENT_ID, AGE_AT_DIAGNOSIS, AGE_AT_PROCUREMENT, RACE, SMOKING, PSA, M_STAGE, VITAL_STATUS, DISEASE_EXTENT; sample: ..., GLEASON_SCORE, GENE_PANEL, 8Q_ARM, TMB) show no income, deprivation, zip or ancestry column; substituting proxies (race, smoking, disease extent) for income is invalid. CHECK: grep all headers and # description lines of every file for income/socioeconomic/deprivation/zip/tract/ancestry/admixture. IF FOUND absent: the exposure cannot be analysed, so the correct label is Not verifiable, regardless of how 8q relates to race. SOURCE: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2823519

label: Race is not ancestry
text: PITFALL: Treating self-reported RACE as if it were genetic ancestry; the hypothesis says adjust for race AND ancestry, and race is a social category not a proxy for ancestry. CHECK: look for a separate continuous ancestry estimate (e.g. % African/European ancestry, PCs); only RACE exists in data_clinical_patient.txt. IF FOUND only race: do not claim ancestry adjustment was done; this further supports Not verifiable for the adjusted claim. SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/cell-genomics/fulltext/S2666-979X(22)00092-1

label: 8q gain definition
text: PITFALL: Deriving 8q gain ad hoc from the seg file with a naive log2 threshold ignores purity/ploidy and panel breadth of coverage, so calls disagree with the provided 8Q_ARM column. CHECK: use the curated 8Q_ARM column in data_clinical_sample.txt (Gain/Neutral/etc.) as the outcome; if recomputing from data_cna_hg19.seg, use an ASCETS-style arm call (fraction of arm covered >=0.7 by segments above ~0.2 log2) and compare agreement. IF FOUND disagreement: prefer the curated column and note it. SOURCE: https://github.com/beroukhim-lab/ascets

label: One sample per patient
text: PITFALL: Multiple samples per patient (T01, T02) inflate n and violate independence when relating patient-level exposures to 8q status. CHECK: count SAMPLE_ID per PATIENT_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt. IF FOUND duplicates: keep one sample per patient (e.g. first/primary) or use patient-clustered models. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9302205/

label: Confounding by stage and sample type
text: PITFALL: 8q gain frequency differs strongly by sample type (metastatic vs primary) and disease extent/Gleason, which confound any area-level exposure comparison. CHECK: crosstab 8Q_ARM by SAMPLE_TYPE and DISEASE_EXTENT. IF FOUND imbalance: adjust or stratify by these in any model (relevant only if an exposure variable exists). SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9701576/

label: Ecological fallacy area income
text: PITFALL: Area-level income measured on individuals invites ecological fallacy and clustering by neighbourhood; even when present, models need multilevel/cluster-robust SEs. CHECK: whether any geographic identifier exists to cluster on. IF FOUND absent along with income: claim cannot be tested. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7493460/

label: WES variable presence
text: PITFALL: Comparing panel TMB to WES TMB requires a WES-derived TMB for the same samples; in this dataset all samples are MSK-IMPACT panel (IMPACT341/410/468 in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt) and no column header mentions exome/WES. CHECK: grep all clinical headers and #-description lines for 'WES', 'exome', 'whole' and check data_gene_panel_matrix and mutations Sequencer/Center columns for any non-IMPACT assay. IF FOUND none: do not fabricate a WES proxy; the comparison variable is absent, which bears on whether the claim can be tested at all. SOURCE: https://jitc.bmj.com/content/8/1/e000147

label: Circular TMB columns
text: PITFALL: MUTATION_RATE and TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS in data_clinical_sample.txt are both computed from the same panel mutation calls (counts divided by panel Mb, differing only by filtering/denominator), so correlating them, or correlating either with mutation counts recomputed from data_mutations.txt, is circular and says nothing about panel-vs-WES concordance. CHECK: compute ratio TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS/MUTATION_RATE per GENE_PANEL; a near-constant ratio per panel proves they are rescalings. IF FOUND: do not treat a high correlation between them as evidence about WES. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9103036/

label: Panel version size
text: PITFALL: Panel TMB depends on panel size and version (MSK-IMPACT 341/410/468 genes ~0.9-1.5 Mb); pooling versions without per-Mb normalisation mixes scales and small panels have large sampling variance at low TMB. CHECK: tabulate GENE_PANEL and compare TMB distributions by panel. IF FOUND: normalise by panel-specific Mb or stratify by panel. SOURCE: https://www.esmoopen.com/article/S2059-7029(20)30188-5/fulltext

label: Panel overestimation vs correlation
text: PITFALL: Targeted cancer panels overestimate TMB relative to WES because cancer genes are enriched for (hotspot/driver) mutations; published panel-WES studies report high correlation (e.g. MSK-IMPACT vs WES in 49 NSCLC tumours, good correlation) but with systematic bias, so concordance claims must separate correlation from agreement. CHECK: if paired WES values exist, report Spearman rho plus slope/intercept and Bland-Altman on log TMB. IF FOUND bias: say correlation can be high despite bias; the hypothesis is about correlation. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11256552/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6249625/

label: Skew and correlation
text: PITFALL: TMB is heavily right-skewed with outliers (hypermutators), so Pearson correlation on raw values is dominated by a few samples. CHECK: inspect distribution and top values. IF FOUND: use Spearman or Pearson on log(TMB+1). SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3576830/

label: TMB calculation rules
text: PITFALL: Bioinformatic choices (synonymous vs nonsynonymous, indels, hotspot/driver exclusion, germline filtering, VAF cutoffs, tumour-only vs matched normal) shift panel TMB. CHECK: inspect Variant_Classification, Hotspot, SOMATIC_STATUS columns. IF FOUND mixed matched/unmatched samples: stratify or restrict to Matched. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.annonc.2021.09.016

label: One sample per patient
text: PITFALL: Multiple samples per patient (e.g. T01, T03 suffixes) inflate n in correlation analyses. CHECK: count SAMPLE_ID per PATIENT_ID. IF FOUND: keep one sample per patient. SOURCE: https://github.com/chris-kreitzer/IMPACT_Prostate

label: Check exposure/outcome variables exist
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis needs three variables (ctDNA detected yes/no, anticoagulation exposure, VTE outcome with timing); the provided headers show only SEX/RACE/ETHNICITY (patient) and CANCER_TYPE/ONCOTREE/TMB (sample) plus genomic tables from the MSK-ACCESS plasma panel, so the outcome and exposure may be absent. CHECK: grep every '#' description line and header of data_clinical_patient.txt and data_clinical_sample.txt for VTE, thrombo, embol, DVT, PE, anticoag, LMWH, DOAC, heparin, apixaban, warfarin, OS/DFS months/status. IF FOUND none: VTE and anticoagulation are not derivable from genomics, so the claim cannot be tested; label Not verifiable rather than inventing a proxy. SOURCE: https://www.jthjournal.org/article/S1538-7836(24)00609-3/fulltext

label: ctDNA proxy is not enough
text: PITFALL: A ctDNA-detected flag can be proxied from mutation/CNA/SV calls in plasma panel data, but having ctDNA status alone does not make an anticoagulation-by-ctDNA VTE claim testable; analysts can be tempted to answer True/False from ctDNA-vs-genomics associations alone. CHECK: confirm that a VTE event variable AND an anticoagulation-at-draw variable exist before running any test. IF FOUND missing: do not substitute TMB, cancer type or mutation counts as stand-ins for VTE; report Not verifiable. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-024-03195-0

label: CH contamination of ctDNA status
text: PITFALL: If ctDNA status is derived from MSK-ACCESS plasma calls, clonal hematopoiesis and germline variants (e.g., DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, PPM1D, TP53 low-VAF, CHEK2) produce false ctDNA+ calls. CHECK: look in data_mutations.txt for matched-normal/WBC filtering columns or annotations, and the share of samples whose only alterations are in CH genes. IF FOUND: define ctDNA+ excluding CH-gene-only and germline calls; run a sensitivity analysis with and without them. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-24109-5

label: Mutation presence is not pathway activation
text: PITFALL: Pathway activation is a functional/phenotypic claim (e.g. phospho-ERK, MAPK transcriptional output), but this dataset (clinical, gene panel matrix, mutations MAF, SV) contains only DNA/fusion calls; finding ARAF N217I/G322S in the MAF shows the mutations exist, not that they activate MAPK. CHECK: list every table and column; confirm whether any expression, protein, phospho, pathway-score or functional-assay variable exists. IF FOUND (none present): presence of the mutations alone cannot demonstrate activation; weigh 'Not verifiable' versus 'True' explicitly and justify which, rather than reading activation off the mutation list. SOURCE: https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pcbi.1006658 ; https://www.nature.com/articles/ng.3593

label: Competing risk of death for VTE
text: PITFALL: In cancer cohorts death is a frequent competing event; Kaplan-Meier 1-KM and plain Cox overestimate VTE incidence and can distort group comparisons, especially when ctDNA+ patients die sooner. CHECK: count deaths before VTE by ctDNA group if survival data exist. IF FOUND: use Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence and Fine-Gray or cause-specific Cox models with death as competing risk. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7279950/

label: Locate ARAF variants exactly
text: PITFALL: Not finding the named variants is easy to misread as evidence against the hypothesis, and finding them as evidence for it. CHECK: grep data_mutations.txt for Hugo_Symbol==ARAF and inspect HGVSp_Short, Protein_position, Transcript_ID, Variant_Classification and which Tumor_Sample_Barcode carries each; also check ARAF in data_sv.txt. IF FOUND: report which samples carry N217I and G322S; if absent, check alternative transcripts before concluding absence. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/mutation-data-transcript-annotation/

label: Confounding by indication and immortal time
text: PITFALL: Anticoagulation in observational data is confounded by indication (prior VTE, AF, high Khorana score) and immortal-time bias if exposure is defined by any later use. CHECK: verify anticoagulation is defined at the plasma draw/time zero and whether prior VTE is recorded. IF FOUND: define exposure at baseline (or time-varying), exclude or adjust for prior VTE and cancer type/stage; do not classify post-baseline users as exposed from time zero. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwm324

label: Transcript isoform protein-notation mismatch
text: PITFALL: Protein-change labels depend on transcript isoform; ARAF positions such as 217 or 322 may differ between Ensembl/RefSeq transcripts, so string-matching 'p.N217I' can miss or mis-identify the variant. CHECK: compare Transcript_ID/RefSeq in the ARAF rows with the canonical ARAF transcript (ENST00000377045 / NM_001654) and check genomic Start_Position and codon change. IF FOUND (non-canonical transcript): match on genomic coordinate/codon, not on the protein string. SOURCE: https://github.com/mskcc/vcf2maf/blob/main/docs/vep_maf_readme.txt

label: Null subgroup claim needs interaction test
text: PITFALL: 'Anticoagulation does not benefit ctDNA- patients' is a null claim within a subgroup; a non-significant HR in a small ctDNA- group is absence of evidence, and comparing subgroup p-values is not a test of effect modification. CHECK: report the HR with 95% CI in ctDNA- patients and a formal ctDNA x anticoagulation interaction test; check event counts. IF FOUND wide CI including meaningful benefit: say it is underpowered rather than proven no benefit; support the claim only if the interaction is present and the ctDNA- estimate is near null with reasonably tight CI. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1016/s0140-6736(05)61026-4

label: ARAF missense default is VUS
text: PITFALL: ARAF missense variants are mostly uncharacterised; under AMP/ASCO/CAP and ClinGen/CGC/VICC rules a novel kinase missense with no functional data is a VUS, not an activating variant; only a few ARAF variants (e.g. S214 region, beta3-alphaC in-frame deletions) have functional evidence. CHECK: note ARAF protein domain of N217 (near the CR2 S214 14-3-3 regulatory site) and G322 (start of kinase domain), and whether any annotation column in the MAF (e.g. SIFT/PolyPhen, oncogenic flags) gives effect calls. IF FOUND: treat domain proximity as suggestive only; do not claim activation without functional or downstream readout. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9081216/ ; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31263281/

label: Mutual exclusivity underpowered
text: PITFALL: Using mutual exclusivity with KRAS/BRAF/NRAS/FGFR2 fusions as indirect proof of MAPK activation is underpowered in a tiny cohort (~8 WXS iCCA samples) and can be due to chance. CHECK: tabulate per-sample KRAS, NRAS, BRAF, ARAF, MAP2K1, NF1 mutations and FGFR2 fusions from data_sv.txt; count samples. IF FOUND: report as descriptive only, no significance claims; do not treat exclusivity in n<10 as evidence of activation. SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/cancer-cell/fulltext/S1535-6108(17)30302-1 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5162102/

label: Multiple draws per patient
text: PITFALL: The data are sample-level (multiple plasma draws per patient, e.g. -T02/-T03/-T04 suffixes) while VTE and anticoagulation are patient-level, so counting samples inflates n and can mix ctDNA status across draws. CHECK: count samples per PATIENT_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt. IF FOUND multiple: pick one draw per patient (first draw as time zero) or use time-varying ctDNA status with clustered SEs. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-024-03195-0

label: Germline/artefact calls in WXS MAF
text: PITFALL: WXS MAFs can include germline polymorphisms (dbSNP-annotated) and duplicated records across samples; a recurrent identical variant across tumours may be germline or artefact rather than a somatic driver. CHECK: for ARAF rows inspect dbSNP_RS, allele counts (t_alt_count/t_depth if present), FILTER, and whether the same coordinate recurs across samples. IF FOUND: flag germline/low-VAF calls and do not count them as somatic activating events. SOURCE: https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Data/File_Formats/MAF_Format/

label: Cancer type confounds ctDNA and VTE
text: PITFALL: ctDNA detection is strongly tied to cancer type and tumour burden (metastatic disease), which also drive VTE risk; unadjusted ctDNA-stratified comparisons confound with cancer type. CHECK: cross-tabulate ctDNA status by CANCER_TYPE. IF FOUND imbalance: adjust or stratify by cancer type (and stage/treatment if available) in Fine-Gray models. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12045112/

label: ARAF weak kinase biology
text: PITFALL: Assuming ARAF is a strong kinase like BRAF; ARAF has low intrinsic catalytic activity (non-canonical APE motif) and depends on dimerisation, so a missense in ARAF does not by default imply pathway output. CHECK: none in data beyond mutation type; note it in reasoning. IF FOUND: avoid extrapolating BRAF-hotspot logic to ARAF variants. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41388-018-0365-2

label: SCLC subtypes need expression data
text: PITFALL: SCLC subtypes SCLC-A/N/P (and Y or I) are defined by RNA or protein (IHC) expression of the transcription factors ASCL1, NEUROD1, POU2F3 (YAP1), not by any DNA alteration, so subtype presence/absence cannot be read from mutation or copy-number tables. CHECK: list every file and column in /biodsa-data for mRNA expression, IHC scores or a subtype annotation (grep -i ascl1/neurod/pou2f3/subtype in clinical tables; library check found none in clinical tables and the files given are only clinical, CNA, seg, mutations, SV, panel matrix, timelines). IF FOUND absent: no subtype variable exists, which points to 'Not verifiable' rather than True or False. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6538259/ ; https://www.jto.org/article/S1556-0864(20)30755-3/fulltext

label: Not-profiled genes are not absent
text: PITFALL: Treating absence of ASCL1/NEUROD1/POU2F3 rows in the CNA/mutation tables as evidence the subtypes are absent; these genes are not on the MSK-IMPACT468 panel (library check: none of them appear in data_cna.txt, while MYC, MYCL, MYCN, YAP1 do), so 'not profiled' is not 'not present'. CHECK: confirm gene membership in data_cna.txt and mutations Hugo_Symbol and the panel in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt. IF FOUND: absence of a gene from the data is missing measurement, not a negative result; do not label True from it. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/ ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/3067

label: MYC-family CNA is not a subtype call
text: PITFALL: Using MYC-family amplification as a subtype proxy (MYCL amp linked to SCLC-A; MYC amp to SCLC-N/P/Y); the associations are probabilistic (e.g. MYCL activation in ~68-80% of ASCL1 cases, MYC in only 10-29% of NEUROD1) and most SCLCs have no MYC-family amplification, so CNA cannot assign or exclude a subtype. CHECK: if tempted, tabulate MYC/MYCL/MYCN amplification counts across PDX/CDX samples, but treat only as indirect. IF FOUND: at most mention as suggestive; it does not identify subtype per sample and should not drive a True/False label. SOURCE: https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.abc2578 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10798698/

label: No miRNA expression in data
text: PITFALL: Treating a hypothesis about miRNA expression (miR-452, miR-766, miR-1180 up in HCA and HCC vs normal liver) as testable on a DNA-only targeted panel study; the bd34 data (clinical, CNA, seg, gene panel, mutations; MSK-IMPACT341) contain no miRNA or RNA expression table. CHECK: grep all files for 'MIR' / 'miR' / expression tables (data_mirna*, data_expression*, data_mrna*); the CNA gene list (341 IMPACT genes) has no MIR rows. IF FOUND (no expression data): the correct label is 'Not verifiable', not 'False'. SOURCE: https://www.jmdjournal.org/article/S1525-1578(15)00045-8/fulltext

label: PDX/CDX do carry subtypes in literature
text: PITFALL: The literature broadly reports that PDX and CDX models of SCLC do retain ASCL1, NEUROD1 and POU2F3 subtypes (multiple PDX/CDX biobanks were subtyped by RNA-seq/IHC), so a hypothesis claiming absence is a priori implausible, but prior knowledge is not data analysis. CHECK: decide strictly on whether the given tables contain a subtype/expression variable. IF FOUND none: answer per the task rules ('Not verifiable' when no relevant variable exists); do not import outside knowledge to label False. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s43018-020-0046-2 ; https://www.science.org/doi/full/10.1126/sciadv.abp8674

label: CNA is not miRNA expression
text: PITFALL: Using copy number (gene-level CNA calls or seg.mean over the miR-452/766/1180 loci) as a proxy for miRNA expression; copy number is a weak, heterogeneous predictor of miRNA expression and miRNA loci are not targeted by IMPACT341 (seg means there are interpolated from sparse probes). CHECK: whether any CNA row or probe directly covers the miRNA loci; whether any expression variable exists to validate dosage. IF FOUND (proxy only): do not label True/False from CNA; label Not verifiable. SOURCE: https://d.docksci.com/exploring-the-genome-wide-relation-between-copy-number-status-and-microrna-expre_5a9b9a1ad64ab2d36a701eb9.html

label: No normal liver group
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis needs a normal-liver comparison group, but the clinical table has only tumour samples (9 Hepatocellular Adenoma, 10 Hepatocellular Carcinoma); matched normals (_N barcodes) exist only as germline sequencing controls, not as measured profiles. CHECK: count SAMPLE_CLASS / CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED values and look for any normal-tissue sample with its own data column. IF FOUND (no normal group): a tumour-vs-normal differential claim cannot be tested; label Not verifiable. SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12864-018-5236-2

label: Subtype calling caveats
text: PITFALL: Even with expression data, subtype calling is non-trivial: ASCL1 and NEUROD1 are often co-expressed, YAP1 is low-level across subtypes, IHC thresholds differ, and PDX/CDX show intratumoral heterogeneity and subtype plasticity across passages, with mouse stroma diluting human signal. CHECK: if any expression/IHC column turns up, check thresholds, co-expression and whether calls are per sample or per model/passage. IF FOUND: use relative-expression (highest TF) rules or published NMF signatures and report mixed calls rather than forcing absence. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1186/s40164-024-00548-w ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8143037/

label: Absence of evidence is not False
text: PITFALL: Concluding 'False' because no evidence for upregulation is found; absence of the relevant measurement (or a non-significant result) is not evidence against the claim. CHECK: before choosing False, confirm a relevant variable was actually measured and a test showed the opposite or a tightly bounded null effect. IF FOUND (variable missing): choose Not verifiable. SOURCE: https://www.bmj.com/content/311/7003/485.full

label: Filter to PDX/CDX samples
text: PITFALL: The cohort mixes PDX samples (SAMPLE_CLASS=PDX, ~42) and patient tumour samples (SAMPLE_CLASS=Tumor, ~27), and SAMPLE_TYPE has inconsistent case (Metastasis/metastasis, Primary/primary); the hypothesis concerns PDX/CDX only. CHECK: filter by SAMPLE_CLASS and normalise case before counting. IF FOUND: restrict any analysis to PDX/CDX rows. SOURCE: https://mskcc-epi-bio.github.io/gnomeR/articles/qa-impact-data.html

label: Proper miRNA DE method
text: PITFALL: If miRNA expression were present, the standard approach is limma/voom or DESeq2/edgeR tumour-vs-normal (paired if possible) with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, testing each of the 3 miRNAs in BOTH HCA and HCC; claiming 'both' from a pooled tumour test is wrong. CHECK: run separate HCA-vs-normal and HCC-vs-normal tests per miRNA with FDR. IF FOUND (any miRNA/group fails): hypothesis is not supported as stated. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6518761/

label: No in vivo response variable means Not verifiable
text: PITFALL: Treating a sensitivity claim as testable without a response variable. You cannot judge 'uniform' or 'heterogeneous' in vivo chemo sensitivity without per-model treated-versus-control tumour volume change, mRECIST class, growth curves or IC50/AUC. CHECK: grep every column of all six files, including the # description lines, for response, volume, growth, IC50, AUC, mouse, xenograft, mRECIST, treated or sensitivity. IF FOUND none: the label should be Not verifiable, not True or False. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1158/1535-7163.mct-23-0471 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6643318/

label: Small n, low power
text: PITFALL: Very small groups (9 HCA, 10 HCC) give low power, so any proxy test (e.g., CNA gain frequency at miRNA loci) that is non-significant cannot refute the claim and a significant one can be a multiple-testing artefact. CHECK: group sizes and number of tests performed. IF FOUND: avoid strong True/False from tiny proxy analyses; correct for multiple tests. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6412612/

label: Prior therapy column is not response
text: PITFALL: Using THERAPY_PRIOR_TO_DERIVATION in data_clinical_sample.txt as if it were drug response. It records the patient's treatment before the tumoroid was derived, not how the engrafted tumoroid responded in mice. Prior exposure is a confounder of resistance, not a measure of it. CHECK: read the column description lines. Confirm there is no paired post-treatment outcome. IF FOUND: do not infer uniform or heterogeneous sensitivity from it. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12636388/

label: Genomic heterogeneity is not drug-response heterogeneity
text: PITFALL: Using genomic heterogeneity (mutations, CNA, TMB differences between tumoroids) as a proxy for chemo-sensitivity heterogeneity. Genomic concordance or diversity does not measure drug response, and genotype-to-chemo-response links are weak. CHECK: ask whether any analysis uses only data_mutations, data_cna or TMB to make a sensitivity claim. IF FOUND: treat it as indirect and not enough to call True or False. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9454968/

label: Paired pt/tm samples, avoid double counting
text: PITFALL: Mixing sample types. The sample table has paired patient-tumour (-pt) and tumoroid (-tm) samples, plus Primary, Metastasis and Recurrence samples, and FFPE versus Fresh preservation. Pooling them double-counts patients and confounds model versus tumour. CHECK: tabulate SAMPLE_ID suffixes, SAMPLE_TYPE and SPECIMEN_PRESERVATION_TYPE, and count unique PATIENT_ID. IF FOUND: analyse per patient or by matched pairs, not per sample. SOURCE: https://www.cd-genomics.com/resourse-patient-derived-organoids-multi-omics-fidelity.html

label: Panel and FFPE differences in TMB
text: PITFALL: Comparing TMB or mutation counts across different IMPACT panels (IMPACT341/410/468) and FFPE versus fresh tissue. Panel size, germline filtering and FFPE artefacts all shift the values. CHECK: tabulate GENE_PANEL from data_gene_panel_matrix.txt by sample group. IF FOUND: restrict to genes covered by every panel, or adjust for panel. SOURCE: https://jitc.bmj.com/content/7/1/183

label: Do not reject on prior belief
text: PITFALL: Choosing False just because the hypothesis sounds implausible. Clinically, rectal cancer response to chemoradiation is heterogeneous, but the data must show the tumoroids' response for a True or False call. CHECK: before choosing False, name the exact column that shows varied in vivo response. IF none exists: Not verifiable. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1158/1535-7163.mct-23-0471

label: coding TERT missense is not promoter
text: PITFALL: Treating a TERT coding missense mutation (or any TERT row in the MAF) as a 'TERT promoter mutation'; coding variants are biologically different and do not act through the GABP-binding promoter mechanism. CHECK: confirm Variant_Classification and position of each TERT row; count how many samples carry it (here n is ~1). IF FOUND: do not run a mutant-vs-wildtype expression test on coding mutations as if they were promoter mutations; n=1 cannot support or reject anything. SOURCE: https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6694/13/5/1147

label: no proxies for TERTp status
text: PITFALL: Using TERT copy-number, TERT expression itself, IDH-wildtype status or ATRX-wildtype status as a proxy for TERT promoter mutation; the proxy is circular (expression) or only correlational (IDH/ATRX mutual exclusivity) and changes the hypothesis. CHECK: ask whether any column directly records TERT promoter status; if not, any proxy is an inference. IF FOUND: report that the hypothesis variable is missing and label 'Not verifiable'; at most mention proxies as context, not as evidence. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1007/s10014-020-00360-4 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5042396/

label: unprofiled is not wildtype
text: PITFALL: In cBioPortal data, a sample with no mutation row for a gene is not automatically wildtype; it may be unprofiled. data_gene_panel_matrix.txt here has samples with mutations=NA. CHECK: restrict any mutant-vs-wildtype comparison to samples with a non-NA value in the 'mutations' column of data_gene_panel_matrix.txt, and also check that the region of interest was covered by the assay at all. IF FOUND: exclude unprofiled samples; if the region was never targeted, absence carries no information. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/3067 ; https://docs.bcbi.brown.edu/codiac-for-health/ursa-ri/datasets/cbioportal-for-cancer-genomics/data-dictionary

label: other TERT activation confounders
text: PITFALL: TERT is also activated without promoter mutation, through amplification, rearrangement, or THOR promoter hypermethylation, and TERTp-wildtype GBMs (~20%, often ATRX/IDH-mutant ALT tumours) differ systematically. So a mutant-vs-wildtype comparison is confounded. CHECK: if a real TERTp variable exists, tabulate TERT CNA (data_cna.txt), IDH1_MUTATION and G_CIMP_METHYLATION by group. IF FOUND: stratify or adjust (e.g. restrict to IDH-wildtype, exclude TERT-amplified samples) and report both crude and adjusted comparisons. SOURCE: https://pure.amsterdamumc.nl/ws/files/159161813/Systematic-analysis-of-telomere-length-and-somatic-alterations-in-31-cancer-types.pdf ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5970234/

label: TERT low expression stats
text: PITFALL: TERT mRNA is low in abundance in RNA-seq and often zero (bimodal across tumours, ~27% non-expressing pan-cancer), so t-tests on raw RSEM values or on z-scores are skewed and dominated by outliers. CHECK: look at the TERT row in data_mrna_seq_v2_rsem.txt for the fraction of zeros and skew. IF FOUND: use log2(RSEM+1) with a Wilcoxon/Mann-Whitney test and also compare the fraction expressing; use raw RSEM, not the ref_diploid z-scores, which are scaled to a reference population, for group comparisons. SOURCE: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/genetics/articles/10.3389/fgene.2024.1401100/full ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/

label: null claim and power
text: PITFALL: Labelling a 'no correlation' hypothesis 'True' because a test came out non-significant, when the test was underpowered or used a proxy; absence of evidence is not support. Note also that the published literature reports TERTp mutations associated with higher TERT expression (a trend in GBM, Killela 2013; strong pan-cancer association, Barthel 2017), so a prior against the hypothesis exists, but it must not replace data. CHECK: group sizes and the effect size with a CI, not just p. IF FOUND: if the variable is missing, use 'Not verifiable'; if it is present with adequate n, decide on the effect size. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms3185 ; https://pure.amsterdamumc.nl/ws/files/159161813/Systematic-analysis-of-telomere-length-and-somatic-alterations-in-31-cancer-types.pdf

label: universal-negative claim logic
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is a universal negative (no CALR mutation in any JAK2-nonmutated MPN), so a single well-supported somatic CALR exon 9 mutation in a JAK2-wild-type MPN sample refutes it; analysts often misread it as a frequency question or label it True because CALR and JAK2 are 'mutually exclusive'. CHECK: Build per-sample JAK2 status and CALR status from data_mutations.txt (Tumor_Sample_Barcode joined to SAMPLE_ID), restrict to CANCER_TYPE/ONCOTREE = MPN, and count samples with CALR mutation and no JAK2 mutation. IF FOUND: Any non-zero count with credible somatic CALR calls means label False; zero only supports True if the samples were actually profiled for CALR. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4222424/

label: CALR mutation types are indels
text: PITFALL: CALR driver mutations are exon 9 frameshift indels (type 1 = 52-bp deletion p.L367fs*46, type 2 = 5-bp TTGTC insertion p.K385fs*47, plus many rarer +1 frameshift variants); filtering a MAF to SNVs/missense or to a single protein change misses them. CHECK: grep Hugo_Symbol==CALR and tabulate Variant_Classification (Frame_Shift_Del, Frame_Shift_Ins, In_Frame_Del, etc.), Variant_Type (DEL/INS/DNP) and HGVSp; positions on chr19 ~13054500-13055000 (GRCh37) are exon 9. IF FOUND: Count all exon 9 frameshift indels as CALR mutations, not just type 1/2. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5288135/

label: Cohort cancer type mismatch with ccRCC
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is about clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), but the provided cohort may not contain any kidney tumours; library inspection found CANCER_TYPE values of colorectal, small bowel and unknown-primary cancers only (IBD/colitis-associated cohort, ONCOTREE codes COAD/READ/COADREAD/SBC etc., no CCRCC). CHECK: Tabulate CANCER_TYPE, CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED and ONCOTREE_CODE in data_clinical_sample.txt and grep all files for 'renal', 'kidney', 'CCRCC', 'RCC'. IF FOUND (no ccRCC samples): the data hold no relevant population, so the claim cannot be supported or refuted; do not extrapolate ITH findings from colorectal tumours to ccRCC, and the label should be Not verifiable. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8478611/

label: MAF lacks mutation-free samples
text: PITFALL: In a cBioPortal MAF, samples with zero mutation calls do not appear at all, so 'JAK2-nonmutated' samples must be defined from the clinical sample list, not from the MAF. CHECK: Take all SAMPLE_IDs in data_clinical_sample.txt, mark JAK2-mutated those with any JAK2 row in the MAF; compare counts of samples in clinical vs MAF (SOMATIC_STATUS, TMB columns help confirm profiling). IF FOUND: Use clinical sample list as denominator; a sample absent from the MAF is unmutated for both genes (if profiled), which cannot generate a CALR counterexample. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/3067

label: ITH needs multiregion sampling
text: PITFALL: Intratumor heterogeneity (spatial ITH) is properly measured by multi-region sequencing of the same tumour; a single biopsy per tumour misses heterogeneity and makes mutations look clonal (Gerlinger 2012 ccRCC multiregion study). CHECK: Count samples per PATIENT_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt and whether multiple samples come from the same primary tumour (library saw 171 patients with 1 sample, 3 with 2, 1 with 3). IF FOUND (mostly single samples): the data cannot establish ITH presence or absence per tumour; absence of observed heterogeneity is not evidence of homogeneity. SOURCE: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa1113205

label: Universal ITH claim and sampling
text: PITFALL: A universal claim ('ITH in all tumours') can only be refuted by showing a tumour that is truly homogeneous, which requires adequate sampling depth and number of regions; failure to detect subclones in few samples is a sampling artefact. CHECK: For any patient with multiple samples, check whether they are the same tumour (primary vs metastasis, SAMPLE_TYPE) and how many regions exist. IF FOUND (few regions, primary-vs-metastasis pairs): treat as inconclusive for spatial ITH; primary-met differences measure temporal/metastatic heterogeneity, not intratumor heterogeneity. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1186/s12885-019-5597-1

label: define JAK2 status incl exon 12
text: PITFALL: 'Nonmutated JAK2' should cover all JAK2 mutations (V617F and exon 12 indels such as N542-E543del, F537-K539delinsL), not only V617F; defining JAK2 status by V617F alone can move samples between groups. CHECK: Tabulate all JAK2 HGVSp values in the MAF; flag exon 12 (codons ~536-547) and any other JAK2 calls. IF FOUND: Report results under both definitions (V617F-only and any JAK2 driver mutation); a CALR-mutant sample counts as counterexample if JAK2-wild-type under the reasonable definition. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6960053/

label: VAF-to-CCF purity and copy number
text: PITFALL: Single-sample subclonal inference from VAF depends on purity, copy number and depth, and different pipelines disagree strongly on subclonal architecture. CHECK: Inspect TUMOR_PURITY, MEDIAN_COVERAGE, t_alt_count/t_ref_count, and CNA at mutated loci before converting VAF to cancer cell fraction. IF FOUND (low purity, missing purity, low depth): do not call mutations subclonal from raw VAF; compute CCF with purity and copy-number correction, or declare ITH not estimable. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7867630/

label: JAK2-CALR co-mutation
text: PITFALL: JAK2 V617F and CALR mutations co-occur in a minority of MPN patients (often low-burden JAK2 V617F), so CALR-mutant samples in JAK2-mutant patients are not counterexamples and must not be counted as JAK2-nonmutated, while their presence does not prove the hypothesis either. CHECK: For each CALR-mutant sample list JAK2 calls and VAF (t_alt_count/(t_ref_count+t_alt_count)). IF FOUND: Exclude co-mutated samples from the counterexample count; evaluate the hypothesis only on CALR-mutant samples with no JAK2 call. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8069892/

label: Targeted panels underpowered for ITH
text: PITFALL: Targeted gene panels (MSK-IMPACT, FoundationOne) sequence only a few hundred genes, yielding too few mutations per sample to cluster into subclones, and mixed panels have different gene coverage. CHECK: Use data_gene_panel_matrix.txt and GENE_PANEL to see panels per sample; count mutations per sample. IF FOUND: subclonal reconstruction from panel data is underpowered; restrict comparisons to genes covered by all panels and avoid ITH claims. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8569188/

label: CALR variant pathogenicity/somatic
text: PITFALL: Not every CALR variant is a somatic driver: in-frame exon 9 deletions, silent/intronic variants, or non-exon-9 changes may be germline polymorphisms or passengers, and counting them can create spurious counterexamples. CHECK: For CALR rows check Variant_Classification, exon/position, Mutation_Status/SOMATIC_STATUS (Matched normal) and whether n_alt_count>0 in the normal. IF FOUND: Base the verdict on somatic exon 9 frameshift calls; note in-frame/other variants separately and see whether the conclusion depends on them. SOURCE: https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/132/Supplement%201/5480/265958/In-Frame-Calr-Exon-9-Mutations-Often-Ignored-but

label: Pooled-normal germline contamination
text: PITFALL: Tumour-only or pooled-normal calling (SOMATIC_STATUS / Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode like s_Normal_Pooled; FoundationOne tumour-only) lets germline variants pass as somatic at VAF ~0.5/1.0, which distorts clonality estimates. CHECK: Tabulate SOMATIC_STATUS and Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode; look for variants with dbSNP IDs and VAF near 0.5. IF FOUND: filter likely germline variants with population databases before any clonal/subclonal classification. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5584341/

label: Filter failed mutation calls
text: PITFALL: Mutation call sets can include failed or filtered rows (e.g. a FAILED status column in data_mutations.txt from Foundation rows), which inflate private/subclonal mutations. CHECK: Tabulate the mutation status/filter columns and Center per row. IF FOUND: exclude failed calls before counting mutations shared vs private between samples. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-020-20055-w

label: ID join and cohort restriction
text: PITFALL: Joining on the wrong ID (PATIENT_ID vs SAMPLE_ID vs Tumor_Sample_Barcode) or patients with multiple samples can misassign JAK2/CALR status; also the cohort may contain non-MPN cancers, which do not bear on the hypothesis. CHECK: Verify Tumor_Sample_Barcode values match SAMPLE_ID; check for patients with >1 sample; tabulate CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED/ONCOTREE_CODE. IF FOUND: Aggregate at patient level for 'patients' claims and restrict to MPN subtypes (PV/ET/PMF/MPN). SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: Chromoplexy needs breakpoint-level junctions
text: PITFALL: Chromoplexy (chains of interdependent translocations/deletions) can only be inferred from junction-level SV calls with both breakpoint coordinates and orientations (ChainFinder input); a cBioPortal SV table with only Site1/Site2 Hugo symbols and fusion labels cannot reconstruct chains. CHECK: list columns of data_sv.txt for chromosome/position/strand fields for both sites and count rows per sample. IF FOUND (no coordinates): do not claim to have detected chains; state that the chain-inference variable is absent and weigh 'Not verifiable' rather than inventing a proxy. SOURCE: https://genesdev.cshlp.org/content/27/23/2513.long ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/blob/master/docs/File-Formats.md

label: SV table may be fusion-only subset
text: PITFALL: cBioPortal SV files often contain only curated fusions (e.g. ETS fusions), not the full somatic rearrangement catalogue, so few rows per cohort is not evidence that rearrangements are rare or non-chained. CHECK: count SV rows vs number of WGS samples and tabulate Event_Info and genes (are they all ERG/ETV fusions?). IF FOUND: treat the SV table as a fusion-status annotation only; absence of chains in it is not evidence against chromoplexy (do not label False on that basis). SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/blob/master/docs/File-Formats.md

label: Seg files lack adjacency information
text: PITFALL: Copy-number segments (seg/CNA files) give breakpoints of copy change but no adjacency: you cannot tell which deletion ends are joined to which translocation partner, so 'deletion bridges' and chains cannot be reconstructed from seg alone. CHECK: confirm data_cna_hg19.seg has only ID/chrom/start/end/num.mark/seg.mean with no junction info. IF FOUND: any seg-based analysis (e.g. multiple deletions on several chromosomes) is at best a weak proxy; report it as such and do not equate co-occurring deletions with interdependent formation. SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-017-1267-2 ; https://github.com/mskilab-org/JaBbA/

label: Interdependence needs a null model
text: PITFALL: Clustered or co-occurring breakpoints also arise from sequential independent rearrangements; simultaneity ('interdependence') must be tested against a null model (ChainFinder permutation null, open adjacency rate / copy-number asymmetry enrichment), and simple Monte Carlo criteria have known false positives (~3.9% of sequential simulations mimic chromothripsis). CHECK: if any chain-like proxy is computed, compare against a permutation/shuffled-breakpoint null within each sample. IF FOUND (no null possible): do not call the pattern interdependent; downgrade conclusion. SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/1471-2164-15-S6-S4

label: Chromoplexy definition thresholds
text: PITFALL: Chromoplexy calls depend on arbitrary operational thresholds (e.g. JaBbA: >=3 low-copy (JCN<=3) junctions, breakpoints within 10 kb of each other, spanning >10 Mb across >=3 discontiguous territories; ChainFinder: closed chains, little CN change), and chromothripsis criteria are applied inconsistently. CHECK: state the exact definition used and test sensitivity to thresholds. IF FOUND sensitive: report the range rather than a single prevalence. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1101/836296 ; https://www.cell.com/fulltext/S0092-8674(13)00212-2

label: ERG fusion is not chromoplexy evidence
text: PITFALL: TMPRSS2-ERG fusion forms either by interstitial 21q22 deletion (~3 Mb between TMPRSS2 and ERG) or by balanced translocation/insertion; a chr21 deletion or ERG fusion alone does not show chromoplexy, and the hypothesis' second part (chromoplexy dysregulates cancer genes such as ERG, PTEN, TP53, CHEK2, NKX3-1) requires linking chain breakpoints to those genes. CHECK: tabulate ERG fusion status (SV table, ERG_FISH_RESULT, ETS_FUSION_SEQ) and whether any data link those genes to multi-partner events. IF FOUND only single-gene events: they cannot support the 'chromoplexy causes dysregulation' claim. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10844642/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6082854/

label: Absence of variable is not contradiction
text: PITFALL: Label logic: 'False' requires the relevant variables to be present and analysed giving contrary evidence; missing junction data means absent evidence, not contradiction. Conversely, prior literature (chromoplexy reported in ~90% of prostate cancers) must not be used as a substitute for analysis. CHECK: before choosing a label, list which hypothesis components (rearrangement chains, interdependence, gene dysregulation) have a corresponding variable in the files. IF none for chains: lean 'Not verifiable'; if chain data exist, test them. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6082854/

label: Purity and assay comparability
text: PITFALL: Low tumour purity and subclonal events reduce sensitivity for deletions and low-copy junctions typical of chromoplexy, and samples sequenced by different assays (WGS vs exome) are not comparable. CHECK: inspect PURITY_ABSOLUTE / WGS_BASED_PURITY_ESTIMATION and data_gene_panel_matrix.txt (structural_variants column) to restrict to WGS samples with adequate purity. IF FOUND: stratify or exclude low-purity samples and analyse only samples profiled for SVs. SOURCE: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/biorxiv/early/2019/09/25/781013.full.pdf

label: Comparator variables present: genomic risk model vs IPI
text: PITFALL: The comparator exists in the data and is easy to miss. data_clinical_sample.txt has PROGNOSTIC_MODEL (described as 'Genomic Risk Model Classification': Low/Medium/High risk, filled for about 750 of about 1000 samples), and data_clinical_patient.txt has IPI (0-5) plus its five factor columns (IPI_AGE, IPI_LDH, IPI_ECOG, IPI_ANNARBOR_STAGE, IPI_EXTRANODAL_SITES), with OS_MONTHS/OS_STATUS. That is enough to compare the genomic model against the established index (IPI) directly, so 'Not verifiable' is hard to justify. CHECK: count patients who have non-missing PROGNOSTIC_MODEL, IPI, OS_MONTHS and OS_STATUS together. IF FOUND: compare the genomic model and IPI head to head on that shared set, rather than only testing whether single genes are associated with survival. SOURCE: https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/146/Supplement%201/5301/555797/Performance-of-molecular-classifiers-relative-to

label: Compare models on the same patients
text: PITFALL: Comparing a c-index or log-rank p for the genomic model on one set of patients with IPI on a different, larger or smaller set gives numbers that cannot be compared, because missingness in IPI and in PROGNOSTIC_MODEL differs. CHECK: work out the intersection of patients with both predictors and OS; compare Harrell's C for each on exactly those patients; get a paired CI from a bootstrap of the difference, or use survcomp cindex.comp or the survival package's concordance() with both fits. IF FOUND (different n): report the paired result on the common subset as the main result. SOURCE: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/manuals/survcomp/man/survcomp.pdf

label: Outperform means paired discrimination, not p-values
text: PITFALL: 'Outperforms' is not shown by both predictors being significant on Kaplan-Meier/log-rank, or by a smaller p-value; p-values depend on group sizes and do not measure discrimination. CHECK: fit Cox OS ~ IPI, OS ~ genomic model, and OS ~ IPI + genomic model on the same patients; compare C-index or AIC, and run likelihood-ratio tests of the combined model against each single model. IF FOUND: the genomic model 'outperforms' only if its C is clearly higher than IPI's (paired CI excludes 0). Adding information beyond IPI (LRT significant) is a weaker claim, and the reasoning should say so. SOURCE: https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/561464/anova-model-comparison-versus-concordance-index-comparison-in-deciding-best-mode

label: Optimism: genomic model fit on the same data
text: PITFALL: The genomic risk model was probably derived from this same cohort, so its discrimination here is apparent (in-sample) performance and is optimistic, while IPI was fixed externally in 1993. A higher in-sample C for the genomic model partly reflects overfitting. CHECK: see whether the clinical-file descriptions say PROGNOSTIC_MODEL was trained on these patients, and whether any validation/cohort split column exists. If the teams rebuild a gene-based model themselves, use bootstrap optimism correction (at least 100 resamples, redoing variable selection each time) or cross-validation. IF FOUND: treat an in-sample advantage for the genomic model as weak evidence; a small edge (for example a C difference under about 0.03) is not convincing. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4297220/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5578404/

label: Prior: genetic classifiers rarely beat IPI
text: PITFALL: Prior evidence shows that when DLBCL molecular/genetic classifiers are benchmarked against IPI on the same cohort with optimism-corrected C, none outperformed IPI for OS (IPI C about 0.66; classifiers 0.56 or lower). Genetic models usually add to IPI rather than replace it. CHECK: in the shared-patient analysis, compare C(genomic) with C(IPI) directly, and do not read the genomic model's significance alone as superiority. IF FOUND (C similar or IPI higher): the hypothesis of outperformance is contradicted or unsupported, which is not the same as 'Not verifiable'. SOURCE: https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/146/Supplement%201/5301/555797/Performance-of-molecular-classifiers-relative-to ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7571794/

label: IPI construction and missing factors
text: PITFALL: The IPI column may be missing even when its five factor columns are present, or it may be inconsistent with them; some patients have only some factors (for example only IPI_AGE). Dropping these patients, or treating missing as 0, biases the comparison. CHECK: recompute IPI as the sum of IPI_AGE+IPI_LDH+IPI_ECOG+IPI_ANNARBOR_STAGE+IPI_EXTRANODAL_SITES (each 0/1; the standard IPI scores one point each for age>60, stage III-IV, LDH>ULN, ECOG>=2, >1 extranodal site), check it against the IPI column, and tabulate missingness by genomic-risk group. IF FOUND: use only fully observed IPI, or do a sensitivity analysis; never set missing factors to 0. Also try the IPI groups 0-1/2/3/4-5 as well as the 0-5 score. SOURCE: https://uwhematology.medicine.wisc.edu/home/international-prognostic-index/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10620582/

label: C-index ties and censoring
text: PITFALL: Both predictors are coarse ordinal scores (3 genomic groups against 6 IPI levels), so many risk scores are tied. Harrell's C depends on how ties are handled and on censoring, and a variable with more levels can gain C mechanically. CHECK: compute C with ties scored as 0.5 for both (the survival::concordance default), and also Uno's IPCW C with a truncation time (for example 60 months); check that the result does not change with the choice. IF FOUND (the conclusion flips): report both and give less weight to small differences. SOURCE: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/sim.9717 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3079915/

label: OS event coding
text: PITFALL: The outcome coding needs care. OS_STATUS is coded like '0:LIVING'/'1:DECEASED' and must be turned into a 1/0 event indicator. The sample table also has a CENSORED column, which can disagree with OS_STATUS. Some patients have survival time 0 or missing. CHECK: parse the leading digit of OS_STATUS, cross-tabulate it against CENSORED, and drop rows with missing or non-positive OS_MONTHS. IF FOUND (inconsistent): use OS_STATUS with OS_MONTHS, and record how many rows were excluded. SOURCE: https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/survival/html/cox.zph.html

label: Proportional hazards check
text: PITFALL: The Cox hazard ratios and the C comparison assume proportional hazards. If risk groups cross over time (common when genomic and clinical risk act at different times), one model can look better or worse depending on follow-up length. CHECK: run cox.zph (Schoenfeld residuals) on the IPI and genomic-model fits, and plot the KM curves for both. IF FOUND: compare time-dependent C or AUC at fixed horizons (for example 2 and 5 years), or use stratified or restricted-mean analyses, instead of a single HR. SOURCE: https://stats.oarc.ucla.edu/other/examples/asa2/testing-the-proportional-hazard-assumption-in-cox-models/

label: promoter variants hidden by coding filters
text: PITFALL: Promoter mutations are non-coding and appear in a MAF only as 5'Flank (or 5'UTR/IGR/Intron) rows; cBioPortal-style or 'nonsynonymous only' filters (dropping Silent, Intron, UTR, Flank, IGR, RNA) delete them and make promoter mutations look absent. CHECK: tabulate Variant_Classification for all rows with Hugo_Symbol NFKBIE BEFORE any filtering; this MAF contains 50 5'Flank and 46 5'UTR rows overall. IF FOUND: base the promoter call on 5'Flank (and nearby 5'UTR) rows; never conclude 'absent' from a coding-filtered table. SOURCE: https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/tqVhYFqWvwo

label: one-effect-per-variant hides NFKBIE promoter hits
text: PITFALL: vcf2maf/VEP assign each variant ONE gene/transcript, so a variant upstream of NFKBIE can be labelled with a neighbouring or overlapping gene's symbol (e.g. as that gene's UTR/intron) and be missed by a Hugo_Symbol==NFKBIE filter. CHECK: grep the all_effects column for 'NFKBIE' (e.g. NFKBIE,upstream_gene_variant or 5_prime_UTR_variant) and also select by genomic window around the NFKBIE transcription start (GRCh37 chr6; NFKBIE is on the minus strand, so its promoter is at coordinates ABOVE the gene end; take the gene's coordinates from its own rows in the MAF). IF FOUND: count those variants as NFKBIE promoter candidates and report them. SOURCE: https://github.com/mskcc/vcf2maf/blob/main/README.md ; https://github.com/Ensembl/ensembl-vep/issues/1509

label: 5'Flank is 5 kb, not strictly promoter
text: PITFALL: In VEP/MAF, 5'Flank/upstream_gene_variant means anywhere up to 5 kb upstream of a transcript, which is wider than a core promoter (usually within ~1 kb, often a few hundred bp, of the TSS); and 5'UTR is transcribed, not promoter. CHECK: for each NFKBIE 5'Flank/5'UTR row report Start_Position, the DISTANCE column, the transcript (Feature/Transcript_ID), and whether it is the canonical transcript. IF FOUND: state explicitly whether variants fall in the proximal promoter; count variants within ~1 kb upstream of the TSS as promoter mutations, and mention more distal 5'Flank ones separately rather than throwing them away. SOURCE: https://dev.ensembl.narkive.com/1y8aAm1i/ensembl-vep-workings ; https://useast.ensembl.org/info/genome/variation/prediction/predicted_data.html

label: Pair samples within patient for HER2 loss
text: PITFALL: Treating any post-trastuzumab sample without ERBB2 amplification as evidence of selection for an ERBB2-non-amplified subclone; without a matched pre-treatment sample from the same patient you cannot tell acquired loss from a tumour that was never (or only focally) amplified. CHECK: Use PATIENT_ID to pair samples within a patient, using IMPACT_PRE_POST (PRE-TX vs POST-TX) and sample suffixes (e.g. YJ-her-XXX-P1/P2/M1a, -T01/-T02). Count patients with ERBB2 amplified pre-treatment and with a post-progression sample, then tabulate ERBB2 status (data_cna value 2, HER2_IMPACT AMP) in the post sample. IF FOUND: Base the conclusion on within-patient paired transitions (amp->non-amp), not on unpaired pre vs post group frequencies. Report the number of pairs and loss events. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1002/ijc.30408

label: absence claim logic and detectability
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis claims ABSENCE, so a single real somatic NFKBIE promoter mutation in a desmoplastic sample contradicts it (label False); zero hits supports True only if the data could have detected promoter variants (non-coding regions sequenced). CHECK: confirm the data contain non-coding calls at all (5'Flank/IGR/Intron rows exist; samples are Exome plus Whole Genome per GENE_PANEL), then count NFKBIE promoter hits per sample. IF FOUND: >=1 well-supported hit -> False; 0 hits with non-coding calls present -> True, noting that exome off-target promoter coverage is incomplete, so 'absent' means 'not detected'. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3926691/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4964598/

label: Spatial heterogeneity vs clonal selection
text: PITFALL: Apparent ERBB2 loss between two single biopsies can reflect spatial intratumour heterogeneity (different region or metastatic site sampled) rather than treatment-driven clonal selection; at least two regions are needed to separate the two. CHECK: For patients with several samples (e.g. P1, P2, M1a, M2 suffixes), test whether pre-treatment regions are already discordant for ERBB2 amplification, and whether ERBB2-negative pre-treatment regions coexist with ERBB2-amplified ones. Compare SITE_OF_TISSUE_BIOPSY and SAMPLE_TYPE between paired pre and post samples. IF FOUND: Count pre-existing ERBB2-negative regions as heterogeneity, i.e. a pre-existing non-amplified subclone that was later selected. Treat amp->non-amp shifts across different sites with caution. Pre-treatment heterogeneity followed by a non-amplified post-progression tumour is the pattern that supports subclonal selection. SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1038/s41467-019-08593-4

label: UV/ETS hotspot promoter mutations still count
text: PITFALL: Recurrent promoter mutations in melanoma often sit at ETS/TTCCG motifs that are UV-damage hotspots and may be passengers; analysts sometimes discard them as artefacts, but the hypothesis is about whether mutations are present, not whether they drive the tumour. CHECK: look at the sequence context (C>T at CC/TTCCG, the UV signature) of any NFKBIE promoter hits and whether the same position recurs across samples. IF FOUND: still count them as promoter mutations (recurrence at one site across samples is evidence they are real somatic calls, not noise); mention the passenger-versus-driver caveat only as a remark. SOURCE: https://journals.plos.org/plosgenetics/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pgen.1006773 ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-018-05064-0

label: Purity false-negative ERBB2 loss
text: PITFALL: Tumour purity and low-level or heterogeneous amplification cause false-negative ERBB2 calls on panel NGS such as MSK-IMPACT, so a low-purity post-progression biopsy can look like HER2 loss. CHECK: For each candidate loss, inspect the continuous ERBB2 log2 ratio in data_cna_hg19.seg (chr17 ~39.68-39.73 Mb in hg19) and HER2_IMPACT_LR, not only the discrete call. Check FGA and mutation VAFs (t_alt_count/(t_alt_count+t_ref_count) in data_mutations) as a purity proxy for the post sample. Compare with IHC_HER2/HER2_FISH where available. IF FOUND: Flag losses in low-purity samples (flat genome, low truncal TP53 VAF) as indeterminate and run the analysis with and without them. Losses supported by a clearly sub-amplification log2 ratio in a sample of adequate purity are robust. SOURCE: https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/jco.2015.33.15_suppl.604

label: cohort and somatic filtering
text: PITFALL: Counting mutations outside the stated tumour type or counting germline calls. CHECK: join data_mutations Tumor_Sample_Barcode to data_clinical_sample SAMPLE_ID and keep samples with ONCOTREE_CODE DESM (note DETAILED_SAMPLE_HISTOLOGY_CATEGORY Pure vs Mixed desmoplastic, and report hits for each); check SOMATIC_STATUS is Matched, and look at the Mutation_Status, FILTER, t_alt_count/t_depth columns (many are '.' in this file). IF FOUND: count only somatic calls from desmoplastic samples; report Pure versus Mixed separately if hits occur only in Mixed. SOURCE: https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Data/File_Formats/MAF_Format/

label: Discrete CNA coding: only 2 = amplification
text: PITFALL: The discrete values in data_cna.txt (-2..2) are algorithm thresholds, and only 2 means high-level (usually focal) amplification. A 1 is a shallow gain, often broad, and is not ERBB2 amplification. Mixing the two misclassifies HER2 status. CHECK: Define ERBB2 amplified as data_cna==2 and cross-check against HER2_IMPACT (AMP) and HER2_IMPACT_LR in the sample table. List samples where they disagree. IF FOUND: Use a single, prespecified definition (value 2 / HER2_IMPACT AMP) and treat 1 as not amplified. Report a sensitivity analysis using the continuous log ratio. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/

label: Define acquired resistance strictly
text: PITFALL: The patient must actually have acquired trastuzumab resistance, i.e. initial benefit and then progression on trastuzumab, with the post sample taken after progression. Samples taken pre-treatment, before progression, or after primary non-response do not test acquired resistance. CHECK: Restrict to patients whose TREATMENT/DETAILS_FIRST_LINE_COMMENTS mention trastuzumab, with HER2_RESPONSE CR/PR/SD (benefit) and a POST-TX sample. Use HER2_TTP_ON_1ST_LINE_MONTHS and HER2_TX_STATUS to confirm progression. Exclude primary-refractory (POD as best response) cases or analyse them separately. IF FOUND: Estimate the loss rate only in the acquired-resistance subset, and state how many were excluded and why. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1002/ijc.30408

label: gene identifier matching
text: PITFALL: Matching on gene identifiers can fail: Entrez_Gene_Id is 0 throughout this MAF, and NFKBIE has the alias IKBE. CHECK: match on Hugo_Symbol, SYMBOL and the Gene column (Ensembl ENSG id), and do a case-insensitive grep for NFKBIE across the whole line, not only Hugo_Symbol. IF FOUND: merge all matching rows before deciding. SOURCE: https://github.com/mskcc/vcf2maf/blob/main/docs/vep_maf_readme.txt

label: Paired test and small-n inference
text: PITFALL: Concluding 'no association' because a test is non-significant in a handful of paired cases (absence of evidence). Conversely, calling it an association without any comparator. Paired HER2-loss studies find loss in roughly 20-35% of trastuzumab-resistant gastroesophageal tumours. CHECK: Report counts (k of n pairs with amp->non-amp), with an exact binomial CI. Where possible compare with untreated/non-trastuzumab pairs, or use McNemar's test on paired pre/post ERBB2 status. IF FOUND: If recurrent amp->non-amp loss is seen in trastuzumab-resistant pairs (and not in controls), that is evidence against a 'not associated' hypothesis. Do not treat a small-n non-significant p-value as support for 'no association'. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-022-08520-6

label: Focal amps not in data
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is compound (KIT mutations AND focal amplifications) but the data tables include no copy-number/CNA/segment file; only mutations, MutSig, clinical tables and a gene panel matrix. Focal amplifications need segmented copy-number data (e.g. GISTIC input); they cannot be inferred from point-mutation calls, and ABSOLUTE_EXTRACT_PLOIDY is whole-genome ploidy, not focal amplification. CHECK: ls /biodsa-data and grep the column headers for any CNA/GISTIC/amplification field; confirm ploidy is the only copy-number-related variable. IF FOUND: Do not use ploidy or mutation counts as a stand-in for focal amplification; state explicitly in the reasoning which half of the claim is testable and which is not, and base the label on the testable part plus that limitation, following the task's label definitions. SOURCE: https://broadinstitute.github.io/gistic2/ ; https://www.genepattern.org/modules/docs/GISTIC_2.0/7/

label: Alternative resistance mechanisms
text: PITFALL: Attributing resistance to ERBB2-negative subclone selection while ignoring alternative or co-occurring genomic resistance mechanisms. Known ones in gastroesophageal cancer include MET/EGFR/KRAS/CCNE1/CDK6/MYC amplification, PIK3CA/PTEN alterations and ERBB2 exon-16 deletion. These can coexist with or replace HER2 loss. CHECK: In post-progression samples, tabulate the emergence of EGFR, MET, KRAS, CCNE1, PIK3CA and PTEN alterations (data_cna value 2/-2, data_mutations, data_sv) relative to the paired pre sample, separately for cases with and without ERBB2 loss. IF FOUND: Report ERBB2 loss as one of several mechanisms. Concentration of alternative-RTK emergence in non-amplified post samples is consistent with selection of an ERBB2-negative clone driven by another oncogene. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11352490/

label: KIT passengers vs drivers / TMB
text: PITFALL: Melanoma is UV-hypermutated, so many KIT calls in a MAF are passenger mutations; counting any KIT variant gives a mutation rate driven by TMB rather than by real KIT driver enrichment. Driver KIT mutations in melanoma cluster in hotspots (exon 11 e.g. L576P/V559, exon 13 K642E, exon 17 D816/N822, exon 9). CHECK: Tabulate KIT variants per subtype by HGVSp/Protein_position and Variant_Classification; compare TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS between Triple_WT and other subtypes. IF FOUND: Report both 'any non-silent KIT' and 'KIT hotspot/driver' frequencies per subtype; when the groups differ in TMB, also run a logistic regression of KIT status on subtype adjusted for log TMB. Triple-WT tumours usually have lower TMB, so a KIT excess there is not explained by burden, but excess in high-TMB subtypes may be. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1097/cmr.0000000000000116 ; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867412007787

label: Panel coverage across paired samples
text: PITFALL: Mismatched gene panels across samples (IMPACT341/410/468, or non-IMPACT YJ-her research samples) can make a gene look absent or non-amplified only because it was not covered or because calls differ by platform. CHECK: Use data_gene_panel_matrix.txt to confirm ERBB2 (and any comparator gene) is profiled in both samples of each pair, and check that YJ-her samples have CNA columns in data_cna.txt with non-NA ERBB2 values. IF FOUND: Drop pairs where ERBB2 is not profiled in both samples, and note any platform difference between pre and post samples as a possible source of discordance. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/blob/master/docs/File-Formats.md

label: Filter MAF to non-silent
text: PITFALL: data_mutations.txt (274 MB, WGS) holds non-coding variants (Intron, IGR, UTR, Flank, RNA, Silent). Counting these as 'KIT mutations' inflates frequencies in every subtype. CHECK: value_counts of Variant_Classification for Hugo_Symbol=='KIT'. IF FOUND: Keep only non-silent coding classes (Missense_Mutation, Nonsense_Mutation, Frame_Shift_Del/Ins, In_Frame_Del/Ins, Splice_Site, Translation_Start_Site, Nonstop_Mutation), and count each sample at most once per gene (drop duplicates across transcripts). Read the file in chunks with usecols to save memory. SOURCE: https://rdrr.io/bioc/maftools/src/R/read_maf_dt.R ; https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Data/File_Formats/MAF_Format/

label: Use provided subtype column
text: PITFALL: Subtype labels exist already: data_clinical_sample.txt MUTATION_TYPE has values BRAF_Hotspot_Mutants (150), RAS_Hotspot_Mutants (92), NF1_Any_Mutants (28), Triple_WT (46), NA (43). If analysts re-derive subtypes, or leave NA samples in the comparison group, the result shifts. CHECK: value_counts of MUTATION_TYPE; cross-check that Triple_WT samples have no BRAF V600/RAS hotspot/NF1 calls. IF FOUND: Use the provided MUTATION_TYPE. Drop NA samples from both groups and test Triple_WT against all other labelled samples, and also against each other subtype. KIT is reported as roughly mutually exclusive with BRAF/NRAS/NF1, so state the comparison group you use. SOURCE: https://gdc.cancer.gov/about-data/publications/skcm_2015

label: Denominators / barcode matching
text: PITFALL: Wrong denominators from sample-ID mismatches and unsequenced samples. data_gene_panel_matrix.txt marks 13 samples as NA (not sequenced for mutations) and 346 as WGS. TCGA barcodes in the MAF (Tumor_Sample_Barcode) may differ in format from SAMPLE_ID (-01 vs -06 metastatic suffix; some patients have more than one sample). CHECK: Count the overlap between MAF Tumor_Sample_Barcode and clinical SAMPLE_ID, and count Triple_WT samples whose panel value is NA. IF FOUND: Make the denominator the samples that were sequenced and have a subtype label; a sample with no KIT row counts as KIT-wildtype only if it was sequenced. Use one sample per patient, or report that duplicates exist. SOURCE: https://rdrr.io/bioc/maftools/src/R/read_maf_dt.R

label: Small counts: Fisher exact
text: PITFALL: The groups are small (Triple_WT n≈46) and KIT mutations are rare (about 5% of cutaneous melanoma), so chi-square approximations break down and a few events can swing the result. CHECK: Build the 2x2 table of KIT-mutant vs subtype and look at the expected cell counts. IF FOUND: Use a two-sided Fisher exact test, and report counts, percentages, the odds ratio with CI and the p-value. If several subtype comparisons are tested, apply BH/Bonferroni correction. Read a non-significant result with a small count as low power, not as proof of no enrichment. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4320046/

label: MutSig is not subtype-specific
text: PITFALL: data_mutsig.txt holds cohort-wide significantly-mutated-gene statistics (MutSig q-values across all samples), not results by subtype. A significant KIT q-value does not show enrichment in Triple_WT. CHECK: Confirm data_mutsig.txt has no subtype column. IF FOUND: Use MutSig only as context (whether KIT is a significant driver overall). Base the subtype enrichment test on the per-sample MAF joined to MUTATION_TYPE. SOURCE: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867412007787

label: No allele counts: prevalence not estimable
text: PITFALL: Clonal selection is a change in clone FREQUENCY (cellular prevalence), which normally needs allele read counts plus copy number and purity (PyClone-style); in this data the t_ref_count/t_alt_count columns of data_mutations.txt are empty for all 18,689 rows, so you cannot get VAF or prevalence shifts from the mutation table. CHECK: count non-empty t_alt_count/t_ref_count values. IF FOUND (empty): do not claim that VAFs or prevalences went up or down; use the evidence that remains (mutations present in one sample and absent in another, and the copy-number tables), and say how much weaker it is. SOURCE: https://github.com/Roth-Lab/pyclone/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4864026/

label: Targeted rows identical within patient
text: PITFALL: In data_mutations.txt, every targeted sample from the same patient has the same number of rows (for example, all SA501 targeted samples have 184 and all SA532 have 144), so the targeted table looks like a list of genotyped sites, not of sites detected per sample. Treating these rows as 'present in every sample' would wrongly suggest there was no selection. CHECK: per patient, compare the sets of (Chromosome, Start_Position, Alt) across the targeted samples; if they are identical, the targeted rows carry no presence/absence information. IF FOUND: base your mutation-level comparison on the whole_genome samples only (T versus X, where both exist) and treat the targeted rows as uninformative. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4864026/

label: Private mutations may be sensitivity artefacts
text: PITFALL: Mutations found only in the tumour or only in the xenograft WGS can come from differences in detection sensitivity (depth, purity, low VAF below about 15%) rather than real clonal gain or loss; in PCAWG, low VAF and heterogeneity explained up to 68% of mutations private to one platform. Here WGS mutation counts also vary widely between samples of the same patient (for example SA531T 481 versus SA531X1 1,514). CHECK: compare WGS mutation counts and private fractions per T/X pair and see whether excess private calls track one sample's total call count. IF FOUND: do not count every private mutation as evidence of selection; require a consistent pattern across patients and recognisable cancer genes, or rely on copy-number evidence. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-18151-y

label: Mouse reads create xenograft-only SNVs
text: PITFALL: Mouse DNA in xenograft samples produces false-positive SNVs that appear only in the xenograft, which could be misread as new clones emerging after engraftment. CHECK: see whether mutations private to xenografts are mostly noncoding or silent, are scattered at low recurrence, or increase with the number of passages; look for whole_genome samples with extreme counts (for example SA531X1-whole_genome). IF FOUND: discount mutations that appear only in xenografts and give more weight to mutations LOST from the tumour (or to segment-level copy-number changes), since mouse contamination cannot create losses. SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-019-1849-2 ; https://doi.org/10.1186/s12920-019-0551-2

label: Matched vs unmatched normal asymmetry
text: PITFALL: The tumour (T) samples are labelled SOMATIC_STATUS Unmatched (no matched normal), whereas most xenograft samples are Matched, so germline variants can be called in T but filtered out in X (or the reverse), faking gains or losses of mutations. CHECK: tabulate SOMATIC_STATUS by sample and look at the dbSNP_RS column and recurrence across patients for mutations that differ between T and X. IF FOUND: exclude dbSNP or recurrent germline-like sites before comparing T and X, and limit comparisons to sites processed the same way. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1186/s12920-019-0551-2

label: Purity scaling of log2 CNA
text: PITFALL: The absolute log2 copy ratio or seg.mean depends on tumour purity and ploidy. Xenografts replace human stroma with mouse stroma, so the human tumour fraction is often higher and CNA amplitudes larger; a T-versus-X difference in log2 amplitude can therefore be a purity effect, not clonal selection. CHECK: compare T and X segment profiles by breakpoint positions and the direction of gains and losses, and test whether X looks like T scaled by a constant (high correlation with a slope ≠ 1). IF FOUND: rescale for purity, or compare discretised gain/loss calls, and count as selection only new or lost breakpoints and events whose direction changes, or subclonal-level (fractional) segments becoming clonal. SOURCE: https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/calling.html ; https://bioc.r-universe.dev/PureCN/doc/manual.html

label: Need noise baseline for T vs X divergence
text: PITFALL: Experts disagree on whether xenografts show selection. Ben-David 2017 reported CNA divergence driven by selection of pre-existing subclones, while Woo 2021 (1,451 DNA-based samples) found differences between primary tumours and xenografts comparable to multi-region variation within a patient, i.e. no systematic evolution. A few small differences therefore do not establish selection. CHECK: per patient, measure the fraction of genome whose CNA differs between T and its earliest X and compare it with a noise baseline, such as two samples from the same passage or adjacent passages (for example the SA532X2A-G or SA501X4A-D replicates in the targeted set, or WGS pairs). label: Segment count is not CNA count
text: PITFALL: Counting raw rows in the .seg file as 'number of CNAs' measures segmentation noise/oversegmentation, not alterations; most segments can be copy-neutral (seg.mean near 0). CHECK: Per sample, compute (a) number of segments, (b) number of segments with |seg.mean| above a threshold, (c) fraction genome altered (bp with |seg.mean|>thr / total bp); compare direction across metrics. IF FOUND: Base the conclusion on called alterations (thresholded count and FGA), not total segment count; if metrics disagree in direction between JP and DCIS/IDC, report that the conclusion is metric-dependent. SOURCE: https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/SqtGhn-AZ4s ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPTomics/bioSkills/main/copy-number/copy-ratio-segmentation/SKILL.md

label: Threshold sensitivity of CNA calls
text: PITFALL: CNA calls from log2 seg.mean depend strongly on the threshold (cBioPortal FGA uses |log2|>0.1; CNVkit defaults gain>0.2, loss<-0.25; many pipelines use ±0.3), so the JP vs DCIS/IDC ranking may flip with the cutoff. CHECK: Recompute thresholded CNA counts and FGA at 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 (and high-level ±0.7/-1.1) for JuP3-JP, JuP3-DCIS, JuP3-IDC. IF FOUND: Only call the hypothesis True or False if the ordering is stable across thresholds; if it flips, say so explicitly in the reasoning. SOURCE: http://cnvkit.readthedocs.org/en/latest/_modules/cnvlib/call.html ; https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/SqtGhn-AZ4s
